acquisitions.title: Disney offers $20M for Character.AI’s scandal-plagued chatbot tech
acquisitions.excerpt: Disney has offered $20 million for a non-exclusive perpetual licence to certain intellectual property belonging to Character.AI, as part of bankruptcy proceedings that commenced recently. The proposed acquisition comes despite Disney having previously sent a cease-and-desist letter in September 2025 accusing the chatbot maker of content theft and of harming children using unauthorised characters. Character Technologies subsequently removed all Disney-owned characters from its platform, and Disney later hired former Character.AI chief Karandeep Anand as its chief technology officer. Character.AI has operated for four years and reported over 20 million monthly active users last year, though the business has suffered due to high development costs and lawsuits. These legal challenges include a settled lawsuit alleging that chatbots encouraged a teenager to commit suicide, alongside ongoing lawsuits from the states of Kentucky and Pennsylvania. Character Technologies has assured users that the platform will remain online during the bankruptcy process, with a potential sale expected to conclude between late November and early December 2026. However, the company noted in filings that transitioning the service to a new buyer could impact platform safety, and it remains uncertain whether Disney or other bidders will ultimately acquire the targeted technology.

launches.title: Figma announces new features to define how agents work on its platform
launches.excerpt: Design platform Figma has announced a new Markdown-based editor and integrations with the Payload headless content management system during its first Config event in India. The updates are intended to help define company design rules, incorporate design and code libraries, and guide both first-party and third-party AI agents. As part of these announcements, the company debuted Figma Specs, a markdown editor that allows users to define their design language simply and reference it alongside canvas elements and FigJam diagrams. This centralized system provides context for design rules so that AI agents can better adhere to them despite the non-deterministic nature of artificial intelligence. Figma also moved its code layers feature into public beta, enabling users to build more interactive prototypes and prompt agents to convert designs into code or modify code layers. Furthermore, the platform is supporting more than 20 new tools with its Model Context Protocol, including Open Code, Dia, Grok Bot, and the Indian AI startup Sarvam. Following its acquisition last year, Payload is now being integrated with Figma Make to generate dynamic websites and manage content directly. Figma noted during the event that India is its largest user market outside the United States, with the platform currently working alongside 40 percent of the top 100 companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange.

launches.title: Meet the five companies competing in the Startup Battlefield finals at Disrupt 2026
launches.excerpt: Following two days of live pitches and demonstrations by twenty startups at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, five finalists have been selected to compete in the Startup Battlefield finals. The finalists were chosen from four distinct categories covering space and physical AI, energy and manufacturing, health tech and life sciences, and enterprise and security. The final round takes place on Thursday at 11:30 am Pacific, where founders will present to a fresh panel of expert judges to vie for the Startup Battlefield Cup and a $100,000 equity-free prize. Among the finalists is Apate, which deploys thousands of artificial intelligence agents to engage fraudsters and waste their time. Another finalist, Flox Intelligence, has developed a camera-equipped wildlife-deterrent system that identifies approaching animals and emits species-appropriate sounds. Intero Biosystems creates lab-grown human intestinal organoids featuring multiple cell and tissue types to improve the pre-clinical testing of drugs and compounds. Industrial Next offers artificial intelligence-driven robotic stations designed to let manufacturers retool production lines in minutes and automate complex tasks. Finally, Satlyt has built software aimed at enabling satellites to share computing jobs in space and improve operational efficiencies autonomously.

launches.title: Amazon CloudWatch announces log routing and chained log parsers
launches.excerpt: Amazon CloudWatch has introduced support for conditional log routing and chained parsers through its pipelines feature. This fully managed service allows users to ingest, transform, and route telemetry data to CloudWatch without needing to manage underlying infrastructure. Log pipelines frequently process a mixture of event types that require different destinations, as well as individual events that contain nested log formats. Conditional log routing enables users to define specific routes that send each event to a designated CloudWatch log group based on conditions evaluated against processed fields. This functionality allows organisations to separate events by criteria such as severity, source, or type, facilitating tailored retention and access controls. Meanwhile, chained parsers permit the application of multiple parser processors in sequence, with later parsers consuming fields produced by preceding ones. An example use case involves parsing a JSON envelope initially before applying a Grok parser to a field extracted during the first step. Combined, these features enable administrators to structure diverse log formats and direct them to appropriate log groups within a single pipeline. Both conditional routing and chained parsers are now accessible in all commercial AWS Regions where CloudWatch pipelines is generally available. Users can configure these new capabilities via the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, or AWS SDKs.

launches.title: Colossal Biosciences announces new AI platform to help accelerate de-extinction efforts
launches.excerpt: Colossal Biosciences has announced a new artificial intelligence platform named GenoMorph to accelerate its de-extinction initiatives. The technology uses advanced three-dimensional morphology, comparative genomics, and developmental biology to pinpoint specific genes for editing when genetic data is severely limited. This approach directly addresses the challenge of working with scarce ancient DNA, such as having only a single dodo genome compared to the numerous woolly mammoth genomes available due to better preservation in colder climates. To construct the platform, researchers gathered developmental data from chickens, quail, ducks, and pigeons, combining it with genetic information and skull measurements from over seventy bird species. The system learns which DNA regions are active during the development of beaks and facial structures, allowing scientists to predict the genetic switches responsible for the dodo's appearance. The company has already identified approximately 2,300 promising DNA editing targets for dodo cranial facial morphology to test in the laboratory. Furthermore, Colossal has developed a system using lipid nanoparticles to deliver gene-editing tools directly into developing bird embryos to observe physical impacts without waiting for a full breeding cycle. The organisation also reported that its Nicobar pigeon colony has reached thirty-six birds alongside the successful creation of essential egg and sperm precursor cells.

launches.title: Amazon S3 is now available on the Vercel Marketplace and v0 by Vercel
launches.excerpt: Amazon Simple Storage Service is now natively available on the Vercel Marketplace and through v0 by Vercel for web and artificial intelligence applications. The integration covers everyday storage, analytics, and artificial intelligence workloads by supporting Amazon S3, S3 Tables, and S3 Vectors. Developers can provision resources directly from the Vercel dashboard by navigating to the storage tab, selecting Amazon Web Services, choosing a bucket type and region, and creating the bucket. Connection configuration and resource provisioning are handled automatically without requiring users to navigate to the AWS Management Console. The integration injects environment variables and uses OpenID Connect to exchange short-lived tokens with AWS Security Token Service for temporary credentials, ensuring no static keys are stored. Users can connect buckets to projects and pull environment variables using the Vercel command line interface. S3 Tables offer managed Apache Iceberg tables for analytics that optimize query performance, while S3 Vectors provide storage for artificial intelligence agents and semantic search. Users can also utilize v0 by Vercel to provision resources and generate working code using natural language prompts. The integration is free of charge, with users paying standard Amazon S3 pricing for consumed resources across commercial AWS regions supported by Vercel.

geo.title: Ukraine to restart strikes on Russian oil refineries, Zelensky says
geo.excerpt:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has announced that Ukraine will resume attacks on Russian oil refineries, accusing the United States of withdrawing crucial support and intelligence-sharing. Zelensky stated he had previously restricted such strikes for three days at Washington's request, while Russia continued to target Ukrainian energy infrastructure. The Russian defence ministry reported that an attempted large-scale attack on an oil refinery in Ryazan was intercepted, resulting in a fire from falling debris. Zelensky noted that dozens of Ukrainian cities had experienced Russian attacks over the preceding day and argued that Moscow had ignored a proposed energy ceasefire announced by US President Donald Trump. 

Zelensky stated that the US had threatened to block intelligence and restricted Starlink satellite services used by the Ukrainian military to pressure Kyiv into halting the refinery strikes. While the speed limits on drone connections initially prompted suggestions of a technical glitch, Elon Musk indicated the decision originated from the Trump administration. Meanwhile, sources in Ukraine's Ministry of Defence confirmed that the military-focused Starshield version had since been restored. During a visit to London, Zelensky met with Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who announced expedited deliveries of British lightweight multirole missiles. Zelensky asserted that he would only halt strikes on Russian oil infrastructure if the US supplied additional Patriot air defence missiles.

geo.title: Long-delayed China-North Korea bridge officially opens
geo.excerpt: China and North Korea have officially opened the New Yalu River Bridge following a twelve-year delay in its completion. The infrastructure project spans three kilometres and is anticipated to function as the primary overland route connecting the two nations. This development forms part of ongoing efforts by both governments to strengthen and improve their bilateral relations. Construction on the bridge finished years ago, but its opening was repeatedly postponed due to a lack of connecting infrastructure on the North Korean side and disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. The crossing links the border city of Dandong in northeastern China with Sinuiju in North Korea. Officials from both countries marked the opening with formal ceremonies, although extensive commercial traffic is expected to ramp up gradually. Trade between China and North Korea has historically relied heavily on older, narrower bridges and maritime routes, which have limitations in capacity. The new crossing features modern customs facilities designed to handle increased freight volumes and passenger movement efficiently. Observers note that the inauguration signals a potential normalisation and revitalisation of cross-border commerce after years of strict pandemic-related border closures enforced by Pyongyang. Further details regarding specific daily operational capacities and toll agreements have not yet been publicly disclosed by either administration.

geo.title: Ukraine resumes attacks on Russian refineries as Zelenskyy says 'we're done'
geo.excerpt: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated on Thursday that his country's military has resumed strikes on Russian energy infrastructure after previously refraining from such attacks to give a proposed US energy ceasefire a chance to succeed. Zelenskyy announced the decision in an interview with the Financial Times, declaring that the block on energy infrastructure attacks was finished following reports of recent Ukrainian strikes on oil processing plants in Ryazan and Saratov. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov criticised the resumption of attacks as conflicting with US peace efforts, though Russia continued targeting Ukrainian civilian infrastructure, including strikes on Wednesday that left 600,000 citizens without power. Zelenskyy criticised the United States for withholding intelligence and restricting SpaceX Starlink satellite access for Ukrainian troops after he declined to abide by the ceasefire. Although Ukrainian forces were blindsided by Russian drones and missiles due to the lack of US intelligence, Zelenskyy indicated he would consider halting energy attacks again if the US supplies Patriot interceptors to defend against incoming strikes. The developments follow US President Donald Trump's decisions to lift sanctions on Russian oil, promise purchases of Russian diesel, and call for Zelenskyy to be replaced. Trump's policy shift has angered European leaders, with Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni describing the diesel agreement as a risky decision that provides a lifeline to Russian President Vladimir Putin while failing to lower oil prices driven by the US war in Iran.

invest.title: AI giant Anthropic woos potential investors ahead of stock market debut
invest.excerpt: Artificial intelligence firm Anthropic has been working to build support among potential investors ahead of an expected stock market listing by highlighting its profit-making potential. The company revealed that its revenue surged by 45% to $16.8bn in the three months leading up to the end of September, following successive quarterly rises earlier in the year. During an event at its headquarters in San Francisco, the firm also reported an adjusted profit for the third quarter and placed strong emphasis on safety protocols. These assurances come amidst warnings from current and former researchers regarding severe risks associated with rapid advancements in artificial intelligence. Chief executive Dario Amodei has previously called for a slower pace of development, and the company recently disrupted attempts to use its technology to aid in the creation of biological weapons. Meanwhile, broader financial markets have experienced turbulence following remarks by Broadcom chief executive Hock Tan regarding extreme investor expectations surrounding AI spending. Additional pressure on global markets emerged after US inflation data showed that price rises accelerated more than anticipated in September, raising concerns over potential borrowing cost increases. Rival firm OpenAI is also reportedly eyeing a major stock market debut, though chief executive Sam Altman stated that his company will not go public this year while it addresses ongoing safety concerns.

invest.title: UK economy grew 0.1% in August, beating expectations
invest.excerpt: The United Kingdom economy grew by 0.1% in August, outperforming a Reuters poll of economists who had predicted a 0.1% contraction. This figure followed monthly growth of 0.4% in both June and July, indicating a slowdown in overall momentum. Production grew by 0.8% according to the Office for National Statistics, while services showed no growth and construction declined by 0.2%. On an annual basis, gross domestic product increased by 2.1% in August, exceeding expectations of 1.7% to mark the highest year-on-year reading since August 2022. Following the release, the British pound rose 0.4% against the United States dollar, and yields on U.K. government bonds fell across the curve. The data arrives as the nation faces a cost-of-living crisis driven by high inflation and energy costs, ahead of the government unveiling its Autumn Budget. Analysts noted that the economic slowdown increases pressure on U.K. finance minister John Healey as he prepares to deliver his first budget on October 28. Experts warned that rising debt interest costs and high borrowing expenses have constrained fiscal headroom, leaving policymakers with difficult choices regarding taxation and spending. While some analysts highlighted ongoing economic fragility and risks to consumer spending, others pointed to continued resilience that has positioned the U.K. as the fastest-growing G7 economy this year.

invest.title: TSMC posts record profit for a sixth straight quarter, beating estimates on AI boom
invest.excerpt: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company reported a record third-quarter net profit that surged 68.7% compared with the same period a year earlier, marking the sixth consecutive quarter of record profits. The world's largest contract chipmaker achieved an operating margin of 58.7%, exceeding the upper boundary of its guidance range and demonstrating strong pricing power driven by the global artificial intelligence boom. For the fourth quarter, the company forecast revenue between $52.3 billion and $54.3 billion, representing a substantial sequential increase and a significant jump from the previous year. Advanced technologies, classified as 7-nanometer and more advanced processes, accounted for 79% of total wafer revenue during the third quarter, with 3-nanometer chips representing the largest single share at 33%. High-performance computing remained the dominant revenue platform at 68%, while the automotive segment registered the fastest quarter-on-quarter growth at 23%. Looking ahead, the chipmaker projects that its capital expenditure from 2026 to 2028 will increase significantly compared to the preceding three-year period to support escalating customer demand. Additionally, the company announced that construction of its second fabrication plant in Arizona has been completed, with equipment installation underway and mass production now scheduled to begin in the third quarter of 2027. The board of directors also approved a cash dividend of NT$7.00 for the second quarter, while free cash flow climbed sharply to NT$476.56 billion.
